title: unified-rollouts: enhance canary/AB/shadow auto-rollback workflow and telemetry
author: Aisha Malik
ci_status: pass (initial e2e flaky failure rerun passed)
description: Motivation: improve safety and observability of unified rollouts by strengthening the auto-rollback engine for canary, A/B and shadow traffic patterns, add multi-metric composite evaluation, expose finer telemetry and add e2e stability guards. Summary of changes: refactor autorollback engine into a pluggable evaluator interface; implement CompositeMetricEvaluator that supports weighted metrics (latency P95, error-rate, semantic-quality regression score) and quorum rules; add a probing/quarantine stage to probe new variants under controlled load; integrate shadow traffic probing with canary weighting so shadowing no longer affects rollout percent but still contributes telemetry; add abort/quarantine manual actions to the rollout API; introduce observability metrics and tracing spans for each rollout step and decision; land e2e tests and local integration harness for the new workflow; update docs and rollout examples. Backwards compatibility: rollout config is backward compatible; new evaluator is opt-in via rollout.policy.autorollback.type="composite". Checklist: [x] refactor autorollback engine; [x] composite evaluator implementation; [x] telemetry & tracing; [x] e2e tests; [x] docs and examples; [x] QA signoff and load test. Impact: safer automated rollouts with clearer signal-to-action paths and reduced false-positive rollbacks. Related: ENG-4021 (autorollback roadmap), ENG-4100 (observability for rollouts).

human_readable_summary: This PR refactors the autorollback engine to support a composable evaluator architecture and lands a composite metric evaluator that reduces noisy rollbacks by requiring quorum across weighted signals. It also adds a probing/quarantine stage to validate variants under controlled shadow/canary traffic, expands telemetry, and adds e2e tests and docs. CI flakiness from e2e timeouts was addressed with longer timeouts and retries. Merged to main via squash.
